**Desiring God**

Find your joy in God with **sermons, books, podcasts, video, and daily articles** from the ministry of John Piper.

Desiring God · https://www.desiringgod.org

**Desiring God** - YouTube

**Classic sermons from John Piper** to help you see Christ clearly and treasure him truly. · The Radical Call of Christ · God&#39;s Feast for the Needy · The Great Banquet...

YouTube · https://www.youtube.com

John Piper and &quot;Desiring God&quot; are fundamentally linked through his influential 1986 book, _Desiring God: Meditations of a Christian Hedonist_, and the ministry he founded based on its core message. Piper&#39;s central theological thesis, which he calls &quot;Christian Hedonism,&quot; is encapsulated in the memorable phrase, &quot;God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in him&quot;.

The book: _Desiring God_

*   **The central argument:** The book challenges the traditional view that following Christ requires sacrificing one&#39;s desire for pleasure. Instead, Piper argues that delighting in God is a Christian&#39;s duty and is the most virtuous path, because the pursuit of joy is what glorifies God most.
*   **Source of inspiration:** Piper credits C.S. Lewis with sparking this theological awakening during his time at Fuller Theological Seminary in the 1960s. Lewis&#39;s observation that &quot;we are far too easily pleased&quot; led Piper to reconsider the nature of happiness and God.
*   **Reconciling joy and suffering:** Later editions of the book address the seemingly contradictory reality of Christian Hedonism in a world of suffering.  
    Piper clarifies that the pursuit of joy is not superficial but can be &quot;tear-stained&quot; and found even in the midst of affliction, as believers rejoice in God&#39;s ultimate goodness.

The ministry: Desiring God

*   **Founding:** In 1994, Piper founded Desiring God Ministries to spread the message of Christian Hedonism.
*   **Core mission:** The organization&#39;s goal is to help people live for the glory of God by helping them find their deepest satisfaction in him.
*   **Resources:** Desiring God provides a vast amount of free content, including:
    *   **Ask Pastor John:** A popular podcast where Piper answers various life and theological questions.
    *   **Look at the Book:** An interactive video series in which Piper annotates and exegetes a passage of Scripture.
    *   **Articles and sermons:** Thousands of free articles and sermons from more than 30 years of Piper&#39;s ministry are available online.
*   **Leadership after Piper:** Though Piper retired as pastor of Bethlehem Baptist Church in 2013, he remains active as the founder and lead teacher of the Desiring God ministry.  
    In recent years, the ministry has begun to develop a new generation of teachers to continue promoting the vision of Christian Hedonism.

Tell me more about John Piper&#39;s personal life

**Thinking**

**Kicking off** 6 searches

**Looking at** 95 sites

**Putting it all together**

John Piper&#39;s personal life is characterized by his family relationships, his journey from a hesitant speaker to a powerful preacher, and his theological growth, often influenced by personal suffering and family challenges

.

Family life

*   **Parents:** Piper was born in Chattanooga, Tennessee, to Bill and Ruth Piper. His father was a traveling evangelist for 60 years. His family moved to Greenville, South Carolina, where he spent his youth.  
    In a 2011 article, Piper wrote about confronting his own racism, shaped by his upbringing in the South, admitting that he took for granted the social structure that demeaned black people. His mother, Ruth, died in a bus crash in Israel in 1974.
*   **Wife:** He met his wife, Noël Henry, at Wheaton College, and they married in 1968. They have five children—four sons and one adopted daughter—and a number of grandchildren.
*   **Parental challenges:** Piper has been open about the struggles within his family, particularly with his son Abraham, who has publicly critiqued evangelical Christianity. Abraham Piper is a popular TikTok creator who has mocked his father&#39;s beliefs and formally left the faith.  
    Another son, Barnabas Piper, wrote a book, _The Pastor&#39;s Kid_, which shares his experience of growing up in the shadow of a famous minister. John Piper acknowledged the painfulness of reading the book, which exposed his own &quot;sins and weaknesses&quot;.

Career and calling

*   **Overcoming public speaking anxiety:** As a child and teenager, Piper experienced severe anxiety when speaking in front of groups, leading him to believe he could never become a preacher.
*   **Discovery of a different path:** He majored in literature at
    
    Wheaton College
    
    , where he was exposed to the work of C.S. Lewis, a pivotal influence on his theology. He was called to ministry while listening to sermons on the radio during a period of sickness.
*   **Education and early career:** He earned degrees from
    
    Fuller Theological Seminary
    
    and the University of Munich, where he received a doctorate in New Testament studies. After teaching biblical studies at
    
    Bethel College
    
    for six years, he became the senior pastor of
    
    Bethlehem Baptist Church
    
    in Minneapolis in 1980. He served there for 33 years before retiring in 2013.

Health and reflections

*   **Cancer diagnosis:** In 2006, Piper was diagnosed with prostate cancer.  
    He responded to the news with a theological perspective, stating that the diagnosis had a &quot;wonderfully blasting effect&quot; on self-reliance and worldliness, and brought him &quot;unusually sweet&quot; times with Christ. He had successful surgery that same year.
*   **Theological response to suffering:** His reflections on his own health and other hardships, including the tragic death of his mother, are a recurring theme in his ministry.  
    He has written extensively on how Christians can find joy and trust God in the midst of suffering, emphasizing that it is not a punishment for believers.
